Introduction

Obidos from Spenego Software LLC is a web-based self-hosted secure information repository for storing and sharing private or confidential information within organizations using fine-grained access control. Due to the digital nature of business operations, every organization will have many pieces of confidential or sensitive information that needs to be stored securely and shared only with the right individual (or group of individuals) within the organization. These digital artifacts include login credentials, 2FA QR/Recovery codes, design documents, contracts, files (any type), contact information (attorneys, insurance contacts, vendors, ..), corporate credit cards, corporate subscription information etc. that span various departments (HR, Finance, Facilities, IT, Executive Office, etc.). Using a templating model, both structured (or predefined) and arbitrary digital artifacts can be stored and shared in Obidos.

Obidos platform gives individual users the power to share or revoke access to information. The individual owner has visibility as to who has access to what information. Administrator accounts have no access to information stored by individual users. Organization-wide AD(Active Directory)/LDAP can be integrated into Obidos so that corporate IAM policies can be enforced.

Obidos was marketed as a commerical product since 2024. Obidos is built on IETF and defacto industry standards. There is nothing proprietary about Obidos. Also, Obidos uses many Open Source libraries. Since the developers of Obidos are consumers and contributors of Open Source software, it is only natural that Obidos itself be opened up to the community. Hence this effort.

Features in Obidos

  1. Easy to use dashboards for admins and users that works with any html5 compatible browsers.
  2. Subordinate administrative accounts can be created for specific capabilities.
  3. Multiple AD/LDAP's can be integrated in addition to local user accounts.
  4. Existing SMTP server/gateway can be integrated for email functionality.
  5. SMS gateway can be integrated for texting.
  6. Email Templates are provided for customizing messages.
  7. Auditing is built in.
  8. 2FA QR Code can be set by users for preventing unauthorized password/passphrase resets.
  9. Built-in credentials management capability. This includes password management and password generator.
  10. Built-in Authenticator (TOTP) app. So 2FA QR Codes can be stored and Authenticator codes can be viewed directly within Obidos.
  11. Built-in notification messaging system. External notifications can be done via email and SMS.
  12. A number of Global Templates are provided out of the box. These include popular formats such as Contact Information, Credit Card Info, Bank Details and 2FA QR Code. You can create additional Global Templates as well as Personal Templates to suite the structure of the artifact you want to store.
  13. One off Items can be created using adhoc templating.
  14. 'Notes' can be created for free format textual information.
  15. Items are stored in Containers. Both Items and Containers can be tagged as Private or Shareable. Tagging as Private prevents from accidentally exposing information.
  16. Items can be created with an expiration. This prevents the visibility of the Item after expiration date.
  17. Update permissions on artifacts can be given to other users by owner of the artifact.
  18. Ownership of an artifact can be transferred to another user.
  19. Group sharing is available. When a new user is added to a group, all information previously shared with the group will be available to the new user. Similarly, when a user is removed from a group, all access that were set on the group will be revoked from that user.
  20. Any type of file can be attached to an Item.

Note that Obidos is neither a File Server nor a Document Management System. However, file sharing is supported as part of sharing digital artifacts (such as a design document or support contract) that are critical in the context of business operations.

Enterprise vs OpenSource

Currently commercially supported enterprise version of Obidos and the OpenSource version have the exact same features.

The commercial versions come with some extras in addition to Obidos software. These include administrative scripts (back up database, upgrade Obidos, bulk import users, etc.), web console (cockpit), SNMP support, professional installation, training and professional support.

Manual Installation from source

Note: manuall installation process is quite involved. Support and installer is available under commercial license. Please contact Spenego Software LLC at https://spenego.com/contacts.html for details.

This guide walks through building Obidos from source and running it on a single Ubuntu 24.04 machine. No nginx, no dedicated service user, just Jetty terminating TLS directly with a self-signed certificate. It's meant for developers and evaluators who want a running Obidos with the least ceremony possible.

Note: This is not the production setup. Commercial customers get the packaged installer (TLS via nginx, hardened service accounts, Cockpit, cron watchdogs, etc). None of that is covered here.

Tested against:

  • Ubuntu 24.04 server
  • OpenJDK 17
  • MariaDB 11.4
  • Jetty 9.4.56

All commands assume you're logged in as a regular user with sudo access, unless a step says otherwise.

TLS is required. The GWT client code reads/writes the system clipboard (navigator.clipboard) for copying secrets, and browsers only expose that API in a secure context: HTTPS. During logout, Obidos clears system clipboard and if transport is not HTTPS, a JavaScript exception is thrown and logout from the app fails.

A self-signed cert is enough to satisfy the browser's secure context check, it does not need to be CA-signed for this guide.

Compiling Obidos from source

sudo apt update
# Install jdk 17 first, otherwise maven will pull a different version of java
sudo apt install -y git openjdk-17-jdk
sudo apt install -y maven

git clone https://github.com/spenego/Obidos.git
cd Obidos

# Remember where the repo lives, later steps cd elsewhere (jetty_base,
# scripts/) and need to refer back to it
export OBIDOS_SRC="$PWD"

# Must set JAVA_HOME 
export JAVA_HOME=$(readlink -f /usr/bin/javac | sed "s:/bin/javac::")

./compile.sh prod

This produces target/Obidos-<version>.war. This is the file we'll deploy as ROOT.war further down in Installing Jetty and deploying the WAR.

Installing runtime dependencies

Obidos uses libsodium (via JNI/libsodium-jna) for its crypto. At initialization, Obidos registers /usr/local/spenego/lib/ with libsodium-jna as the only place to look for the native library. This is intentional, not a fallback, so it doesn't matter that apt's own copy is elsewhere and registered with ldconfig. libsodium-jna never searches the standard system library paths here, the .so file has to actually exist at that exact path.

sudo apt install -y libsodium-dev unzip

sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/spenego/lib
sudo cp /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsodium.so /usr/local/spenego/lib/libsodium.so

(libsodium-dev is what provides that unversioned libsodium.so symlink, libsodium23, which actually holds the code, comes along as its dependency.)

Setting up the database

cd "$OBIDOS_SRC/scripts"
sudo ./install-mariadb

What this does:

  • Creates /usr/local/spenego/obidos, then chowns all of /usr/local/spenego to nobody with go+rx permissions.
  • Runs ./GenObidosJdbc_linux (no arguments). This writes the encrypted connection file to /usr/local/spenego/obidos/jdbc.xml (a path hardcoded inside the binary, not something you can relocate) and prints the generated (random) password and connection details to stdout in the form hostname:...|port:...|dbname:...|username:...|password:....
  • Installs mariadb-server via apt, enables and starts the service.
  • Grants privileges to the generated DB user (obidos/obidos) and loads init_db.sql + local.sql as root (MariaDB's default unix_socket auth lets root connect passwordlessly when run as root).

You don't need to write down the password it prints. The app reads it back out of jdbc.xml at runtime. If you ever need to see it again later, e.g. to poke the database by hand with the mariadb CLI, run ./scripts/DecryptObidosJdbc_linux, which decrypts the existing jdbc.xml without generating a new password.

Default login after setup: username admin, password admin, with a forced password change on first login (this comes from local.sql).

Note: local.sql sets system_config.server_port = 443 and fqdn = "localhost". This guide serves HTTPS on 8443 instead (see Installing Jetty and deploying the WAR), so any feature that builds an absolute URL (e.g. password reset emails) will reference the wrong port until you update the Https Port field under Settings > System Settings after logging in. Update fqdn too if you're accessing the server by IP or a real hostname rather than localhost.

Reclaiming ownership of the install directory

install-mariadb deliberately locks /usr/local/spenego down to nobody after generating jdbc.xml, so nothing else needs write access to it by default. For this dev setup, Jetty will run as your own user, so reclaim it:

sudo chown -R "$USER":"$USER" /usr/local/spenego

Installing Jetty and deploying the WAR

export JETTY_HOME=/usr/local/spenego/jetty_home
export JETTY_BASE=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base

mkdir -p "$JETTY_HOME"
tar -xzf "$OBIDOS_SRC/dist/obidos/jetty_dist.tar.gz" -C "$JETTY_HOME" --strip-components=1

mkdir -p "$JETTY_BASE"
cd "$JETTY_BASE"
# start.d/ must exist *before* --add-to-start runs, otherwise Jetty falls
# back to writing everything into one monolithic start.ini instead of
# per-module files in start.d/, and start.d/ never gets created at all
mkdir -p "$JETTY_BASE/start.d"
java -jar "$JETTY_HOME/start.jar" --add-to-start=ssl,https,deploy,jsp,ext,resources,console-capture

That last command is Jetty's own bootstrap mechanism. It creates webapps/, lib/ext/, logs/, etc/, and the start.d/*.ini files for the modules you asked for: TLS connector, WAR auto-deploy, JSP support, an extra jars directory, and console log capture. No plain HTTP module is enabled, see the TLS note in the Install section for why.

Generating a self-signed certificate

Find the machine's IP address, this is what you'll put in the certificate and later type into the browser's address bar:

ip a

Look for the inet line under your active network interface (e.g. eth0 or enp0s3), not lo (the loopback interface, 127.0.0.1). For example, inet 192.168.1.213/24 ... means your IP address is 192.168.1.213.

The --add-to-start=ssl step above already copied Jetty's own demo keystore to $JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore. Remove it first, otherwise keytool will try to open it with the demo keystore's own password instead of creating a fresh one, and fail with "Keystore was tampered with, or password was incorrect":

rm -f "$JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore"
keytool -genkeypair -alias jetty -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 3650 \
  -storetype PKCS12 -storepass changeit -keypass changeit \
  -keystore "$JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore" \
  -dname "CN=<IP-address>, OU=Obidos Eval, O=Obidos, L=NA, ST=NA, C=US"

Replace <IP-address> with the IP address you found above. Browsers will still show a "connection is not private" warning for a self-signed cert, that's expected, click through it (e.g. Advanced, then Proceed).

Point Jetty's SSL module at this keystore and bind it for remote access, the module's default only binds 127.0.0.1:

cat > "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos-ssl.ini" <<'EOF'
jetty.ssl.host=0.0.0.0
jetty.ssl.port=8443
jetty.sslContext.keyStorePassword=changeit
jetty.sslContext.keyManagerPassword=changeit
EOF

Now add the JVM flags Obidos needs, and deploy the WAR:

cat > "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos.ini" <<'EOF'
--exec
--add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens=java.base/java.lang.reflect=ALL-UNNAMED
EOF

Note: Jetty's start.jar forks a child JVM to actually run the server. If you pass --add-opens on the command line instead, the child JVM never sees it. These flags only take effect when they come from a start.ini/start.d file combined with --exec, which tells Jetty to build the child JVM's command line to include them.

cp "$OBIDOS_SRC"/target/Obidos-*.war "$JETTY_BASE/webapps/ROOT.war"
cp "$OBIDOS_SRC/dist/obidos/lib/javax.servlet-api-3.1.0.jar" "$JETTY_BASE/lib/ext/"

mkdir -p /usr/local/spenego/obidos/DataStore

Notice, scripts/fix_war.bash is not needed here. It patches the WAR's cookie domain to work around a double-cookie bug that only happens when both Jetty and a reverse proxy (nginx) set cookies. Since this guide talks to Jetty directly with no proxy in front, skip it, only run it if you later put this behind nginx.

Note: If Jetty fails to start or logging looks broken, the production jetty_base bundles a specific log4j + slf4j-log4j12 binding (lib/log4j/log4j-1.2.17.jar, lib/slf4j/slf4j-log4j12-1.7.25.jar) instead of Jetty's default logging module. If you hit NoClassDefFoundError related to log4j/slf4j, copy those two jars into $JETTY_BASE/lib/ext/ too.

Running Jetty as a systemd service

sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/obidos.service > /dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=Obidos (Jetty)
After=network.target mariadb.service
Requires=mariadb.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=$USER
Environment=JETTY_HOME=/usr/local/spenego/jetty_home
Environment=JETTY_BASE=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base
WorkingDirectory=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base
ExecStart=/usr/bin/java -jar \${JETTY_HOME}/start.jar
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
  • Start the service
sudo sed -i 's/sslMode=trust/sslMode=disable/g' /usr/local/spenego/obidos/jdbc.xml
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now obidos

Logging in

Point a browser at:

https://<IP-address>:8443/

Use the same IP address you put in the certificate's CN earlier. Accept the self-signed certificate warning, then:

  • Username: admin
  • Password: admin
  • You'll be forced to set a new password on first login.

For an actual production deployment (CA-signed cert via nginx, hardened service account, Cockpit, cron watchdogs, etc), use the commercial installer instead of extending this guide.

Changing the Jetty port

To serve on a port other than 8443, edit jetty.ssl.port in $JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos-ssl.ini (created in Generating a self-signed certificate):

sudo sed -i 's/jetty.ssl.port=8443/jetty.ssl.port=<new-port>/' "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos-ssl.ini"
sudo systemctl restart obidos

local.sql also set system_config.server_port = 443, which this guide already overrides to 8443 (see the note in Setting up the database). Update the Https Port field under Settings > System Settings to match your new port, otherwise features that build absolute URLs (e.g. password reset emails) will reference the wrong port.

GWT Super Dev Mode

Obidos uses GWT for frontend. The app can be debugged using Super Dev Mode. Requires tmux.

Look at HOW_TO_COMPILE.txt for details.

This guide walks through building Obidos from source and running it on a single Ubuntu 24.04 machine. No nginx, no dedicated service user, just Jetty terminating TLS directly with a self-signed certificate. It's meant for developers and evaluators who want a running Obidos with the least ceremony possible. Note: This is not the production setup. Commercial customers get the packaged installer (TLS via nginx, hardened service accounts, Cockpit, cron watchdogs, etc). None of that is covered here. Tested against: Ubuntu 24.04 server OpenJDK 17 MariaDB 11.4 Jetty 9.4.56 All commands assume you're logged in as a regular user with sudo access, unless a step says otherwise. TLS is required. The GWT client code reads/writes the system clipboard (navigator.clipboard) for copying secrets, and browsers only expose that API in a secure context: HTTPS. During logout, Obidos clears system clipboard and if transport is not HTTPS, a JavaScript exception is thrown and logout from the app fails. A self-signed cert is enough to satisfy the browser's secure context check, it does not need to be CA-signed for this guide. Compiling Obidos from source sudo apt update # Install jdk 17 first, otherwise maven will pull a different version of java sudo apt install -y git openjdk-17-jdk sudo apt install -y maven git clone https://github.com/spenego/Obidos.git cd Obidos # Remember where the repo lives, later steps cd elsewhere (jetty_base, # scripts/) and need to refer back to it export OBIDOS_SRC="$PWD" # Must set JAVA_HOME export JAVA_HOME=$(readlink -f /usr/bin/javac | sed "s:/bin/javac::") ./compile.sh prod This produces target/Obidos-<version>.war. This is the file we'll deploy as ROOT.war further down in Installing Jetty and deploying the WAR. Installing runtime dependencies Obidos uses libsodium (via JNI/libsodium-jna) for its crypto. At initialization, Obidos registers /usr/local/spenego/lib/ with libsodium-jna as the only place to look for the native library. This is intentional, not a fallback, so it doesn't matter that apt's own copy is elsewhere and registered with ldconfig. libsodium-jna never searches the standard system library paths here, the .so file has to actually exist at that exact path. sudo apt install -y libsodium-dev unzip sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/spenego/lib sudo cp /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsodium.so /usr/local/spenego/lib/libsodium.so (libsodium-dev is what provides that unversioned libsodium.so symlink, libsodium23, which actually holds the code, comes along as its dependency.) Setting up the database cd "$OBIDOS_SRC/scripts" sudo ./install-mariadb What this does: Creates /usr/local/spenego/obidos, then chowns all of /usr/local/spenego to nobody with go+rx permissions. Runs ./GenObidosJdbc_linux (no arguments). This writes the encrypted connection file to /usr/local/spenego/obidos/jdbc.xml (a path hardcoded inside the binary, not something you can relocate) and prints the generated (random) password and connection details to stdout in the form hostname:...|port:...|dbname:...|username:...|password:.... Installs mariadb-server via apt, enables and starts the service. Grants privileges to the generated DB user (obidos/obidos) and loads init_db.sql + local.sql as root (MariaDB's default unix_socket auth lets root connect passwordlessly when run as root). You don't need to write down the password it prints. The app reads it back out of jdbc.xml at runtime. If you ever need to see it again later, e.g. to poke the database by hand with the mariadb CLI, run ./scripts/DecryptObidosJdbc_linux, which decrypts the existing jdbc.xml without generating a new password. Default login after setup: username admin, password admin, with a forced password change on first login (this comes from local.sql). Note: local.sql sets system_config.server_port = 443 and fqdn = "localhost". This guide serves HTTPS on 8443 instead (see Installing Jetty and deploying the WAR), so any feature that builds an absolute URL (e.g. password reset emails) will reference the wrong port until you update the Https Port field under Settings > System Settings after logging in. Update fqdn too if you're accessing the server by IP or a real hostname rather than localhost. Reclaiming ownership of the install directory install-mariadb deliberately locks /usr/local/spenego down to nobody after generating jdbc.xml, so nothing else needs write access to it by default. For this dev setup, Jetty will run as your own user, so reclaim it: sudo chown -R "$USER":"$USER" /usr/local/spenego Installing Jetty and deploying the WAR export JETTY_HOME=/usr/local/spenego/jetty_home export JETTY_BASE=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base mkdir -p "$JETTY_HOME" tar -xzf "$OBIDOS_SRC/dist/obidos/jetty_dist.tar.gz" -C "$JETTY_HOME" --strip-components=1 mkdir -p "$JETTY_BASE" cd "$JETTY_BASE" # start.d/ must exist *before* --add-to-start runs, otherwise Jetty falls # back to writing everything into one monolithic start.ini instead of # per-module files in start.d/, and start.d/ never gets created at all mkdir -p "$JETTY_BASE/start.d" java -jar "$JETTY_HOME/start.jar" --add-to-start=ssl,https,deploy,jsp,ext,resources,console-capture That last command is Jetty's own bootstrap mechanism. It creates webapps/, lib/ext/, logs/, etc/, and the start.d/*.ini files for the modules you asked for: TLS connector, WAR auto-deploy, JSP support, an extra jars directory, and console log capture. No plain HTTP module is enabled, see the TLS note in the Install section for why. Generating a self-signed certificate Find the machine's IP address, this is what you'll put in the certificate and later type into the browser's address bar: ip a Look for the inet line under your active network interface (e.g. eth0 or enp0s3), not lo (the loopback interface, 127.0.0.1). For example, inet 192.168.1.213/24 ... means your IP address is 192.168.1.213. The --add-to-start=ssl step above already copied Jetty's own demo keystore to $JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore. Remove it first, otherwise keytool will try to open it with the demo keystore's own password instead of creating a fresh one, and fail with "Keystore was tampered with, or password was incorrect": rm -f "$JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore" keytool -genkeypair -alias jetty -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 3650 \ -storetype PKCS12 -storepass changeit -keypass changeit \ -keystore "$JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore" \ -dname "CN=<IP-address>, OU=Obidos Eval, O=Obidos, L=NA, ST=NA, C=US" Replace <IP-address> with the IP address you found above. Browsers will still show a "connection is not private" warning for a self-signed cert, that's expected, click through it (e.g. Advanced, then Proceed). Point Jetty's SSL module at this keystore and bind it for remote access, the module's default only binds 127.0.0.1: cat > "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos-ssl.ini" <<'EOF' jetty.ssl.host=0.0.0.0 jetty.ssl.port=8443 jetty.sslContext.keyStorePassword=changeit jetty.sslContext.keyManagerPassword=changeit EOF Now add the JVM flags Obidos needs, and deploy the WAR: cat > "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos.ini" <<'EOF' --exec --add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED --add-opens=java.base/java.lang.reflect=ALL-UNNAMED EOF Note: Jetty's start.jar forks a child JVM to actually run the server. If you pass --add-opens on the command line instead, the child JVM never sees it. These flags only take effect when they come from a start.ini/start.d file combined with --exec, which tells Jetty to build the child JVM's command line to include them. cp "$OBIDOS_SRC"/target/Obidos-*.war "$JETTY_BASE/webapps/ROOT.war" cp "$OBIDOS_SRC/dist/obidos/lib/javax.servlet-api-3.1.0.jar" "$JETTY_BASE/lib/ext/" mkdir -p /usr/local/spenego/obidos/DataStore Notice, scripts/fix_war.bash is not needed here. It patches the WAR's cookie domain to work around a double-cookie bug that only happens when both Jetty and a reverse proxy (nginx) set cookies. Since this guide talks to Jetty directly with no proxy in front, skip it, only run it if you later put this behind nginx. Note: If Jetty fails to start or logging looks broken, the production jetty_base bundles a specific log4j + slf4j-log4j12 binding (lib/log4j/log4j-1.2.17.jar, lib/slf4j/slf4j-log4j12-1.7.25.jar) instead of Jetty's default logging module. If you hit NoClassDefFoundError related to log4j/slf4j, copy those two jars into $JETTY_BASE/lib/ext/ too. Running Jetty as a systemd service sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/obidos.service > /dev/null <<EOF [Unit] Description=Obidos (Jetty) After=network.target mariadb.service Requires=mariadb.service blocks.html_en: Obidos from Spenego Software LLC is a web-based self-hosted secure information repository for storing and sharing private or confidential information within organizations using fine-grained access control. Due to the digital nature of business operations, every organization will have many pieces of confidential or sensitive information that needs to be stored securely and shared only with the right individual (or group of individuals) within the organization. These digital artifacts include login credentials, 2FA QR/Recovery codes, design documents, contracts, files (any type), contact information (attorneys, insurance contacts, vendors, ..), corporate credit cards, corporate subscription information etc. that span various departments (HR, Finance, Facilities, IT, Executive Office, etc.). Using a templating model, both structured (or predefined) and arbitrary digital artifacts can be stored and shared in Obidos.

介绍

Spenego Software LLC 的 Obidos 是一个基于 Web 的自托管安全信息存储库，用于使用细粒度访问控制在组织内存储和共享私人或机密信息。 由于业务运营的数字化性质，每个组织都会拥有许多机密或敏感信息，需要安全存储这些信息，并仅与组织内合适的个人（或个人群体）共享。 这些数字工件包括跨越各个部门（人力资源、财务、设施、IT、行政办公室等）的登录凭据、2FA QR/恢复码、设计文档、合同、文件（任何类型）、联系信息（律师、保险联系人、供应商等）、公司信用卡、公司订阅信息等。 使用模板模型，结构化（或预定义）和任意数字工件都可以在 Obidos 中存储和共享。

Obidos 平台赋予个人用户共享或撤销信息访问权限的权力。 个人所有者可以了解谁有权访问哪些信息。 管理员帐户无权访问单个用户存储的信息。 组织范围内的 AD(Active Directory)/LDAP 可以集成到 Obidos 中，以便执行企业 IAM 策略。

Obidos 自 2024 年起作为商业产品上市。 Obidos 基于 IETF 和事实上的行业标准构建。 Obidos 没有任何专有内容。 此外，Obidos 使用许多开源库。 由于 Obidos 的开发者是开源软件的消费者和贡献者，Obidos 本身向社区开放是很自然的。 因此才有了这一努力。

奥比都斯特色

  1. 管理员和用户易于使用的仪表板，可与任何 html5 兼容的浏览器配合使用。
  2. 可以为特定功能创建从属管理帐户。
  3. 除了本地用户帐户之外，还可以集成多个 AD/LDAP。
  4. 可以集成现有的 SMTP 服务器/网关来实现电子邮件功能。
  5. 可以集成短信网关来发送短信。
  6. 提供电子邮件模板用于自定义消息。
  7. 审计是内置的。
  8. 用户可以设置 2FA QR 码，以防止未经授权的密码/密码重置。
  9. 内置凭证管理功能。 这包括密码管理和密码生成器。
  10. 内置身份验证器 (TOTP) 应用程序。 因此，可以存储 2FA QR 码，并且可以直接在 Obidos 中查看验证器代码。
  11. 内置通知消息系统。 外部通知可以通过电子邮件和短信完成。
  12. 开箱即用地提供了许多全局模板。 其中包括联系信息、信用卡信息、银行详细信息和 2FA 二维码等流行格式。 您可以创建其他全局模板以及个人模板来适应您要存储的工件的结构。
  13. 可以使用临时模板创建一次性项目。
  14. 可以为自由格式的文本信息创建“注释”。
  15. 物品存储在容器中。 项目和容器都可以标记为私有或可共享。 标记为私人可防止意外泄露信息。
  16. 创建的项目可以有期限。 这可以防止该项目在过期日期后可见。
  17. 工件的更新权限可以由工件的所有者授予其他用户。
  18. 工件的所有权可以转移给另一个用户。
  19. 可以进行群组共享。 当新用户添加到群组时，之前与该群组共享的所有信息都将可供新用户使用。 同样，当用户从组中删除时，该用户对该组设置的所有访问权限都将被撤销。
  20. 任何类型的文件都可以附加到项目。

请注意，Obidos 既不是文件服务器也不是文档管理系统。 但是，文件共享作为共享数字工件（例如设计文档或支持合同）的一部分受到支持，这在业务运营环境中至关重要。

本指南逐步介绍从源代码构建 Obidos 并在单个 Ubuntu 24.04 计算机上运行它。 没有 nginx，没有专用服务用户，只是 Jetty 使用自签名证书直接终止 TLS。 它适用于希望以尽可能少的仪式运行 Obidos 的开发人员和评估人员。

注意：这不是生产设置。 商业客户获得打包的安装程序（通过 nginx 进行 TLS、强化服务帐户、Cockpit、cron 看门狗等）。 这里没有涵盖这些内容。

测试针对：

  • Ubuntu 24.04 服务器
  • OpenJDK 17
  • 玛丽亚数据库 11.4
  • Jetty 9.4.56

所有命令都假设您以具有 sudo 访问权限的普通用户身份登录，除非步骤另有说明。

需要 TLS。 GWT 客户端代码读取/写入系统剪贴板 (navigator.clipboard) 以复制机密，浏览器仅在安全上下文中公开该 API：HTTPS。 注销期间，Obidos 会清除系统剪贴板，如果传输不是 HTTPS，则会引发 JavaScript 异常，并且从应用程序注销失败。

自签名证书足以满足浏览器的安全上下文检查，本指南不需要对其进行 CA 签名。

从源代码编译 Obidos

sudo apt update
# Install jdk 17 first, otherwise maven will pull a different version of java
sudo apt install -y git openjdk-17-jdk
sudo apt install -y maven

git clone https://github.com/spenego/Obidos.git
cd Obidos

# Remember where the repo lives, later steps cd elsewhere (jetty_base,
# scripts/) and need to refer back to it
export OBIDOS_SRC="$PWD"

# Must set JAVA_HOME 
export JAVA_HOME=$(readlink -f /usr/bin/javac | sed "s:/bin/javac::")

./compile.sh prod

这会生成 target/Obidos-<version>.war。 这是我们将在安装 Jetty 和部署 WAR 中部署为 ROOT.war 的文件。

安装运行时依赖项

Obidos 使用 libsodium（通过 JNI/libsodium-jna）进行加密。 在初始化时，Obidos 将 /usr/local/spenego/lib/ 与 libsodium-jna 注册为查找本机库的唯一位置。 这是故意的，而不是后备，因此 apt 自己的副本在其他地方并使用 ldconfig 注册并不重要。 libsodium-jna 永远不会在这里搜索标准系统库路径，.so 文件必须实际存在于该确切路径中。

sudo apt install -y libsodium-dev unzip

sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/spenego/lib
sudo cp /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsodium.so /usr/local/spenego/lib/libsodium.so

（libsodium-dev 提供了未版本化的 libsodium.so 符号链接，libsodium23 实际上保存了代码，作为其依赖项出现。）

设置数据库

cd "$OBIDOS_SRC/scripts"
sudo ./install-mariadb

这是做什么的：

  • 创建 /usr/local/spenego/obidos，然后将所有 /usr/local/spenego chown 给任何具有 go+rx 权限的人。
  • 运行 ./GenObidosJdbc_linux （无参数）。 这会将加密的连接文件写入 /usr/local/spenego/obidos/jdbc.xml （二进制文件中硬编码的路径，无法重新定位），并将生成的（随机）密码和连接详细信息以主机名:...|端口:...|数据库名:...|用户名:...|密码:.... 的形式打印到标准输出。
  • 通过 apt 安装 mariadb-server，启用并启动该服务。
  • 向生成的数据库用户 (obidos/obidos) 授予权限，并以 root 身份加载 init_db.sql + local.sql（MariaDB 的默认 unix_socket auth 允许 root 在以 root 身份运行时进行无密码连接）。

您不需要写下它打印的密码。 应用程序在运行时从 jdbc.xml 中读回它。 如果您以后需要再次查看它，例如要使用 mariadb CLI 手动查看数据库，请运行 ./scripts/DecryptObidosJdbc_linux，这会解密现有的 jdbc.xml 而不生成新密码。

设置后默认登录：用户名 admin，密码 admin，首次登录时强制更改密码（来自 local.sql）。

注意：local.sql 设置 system_config.server_port = 443 和 fqdn =“localhost”。 本指南在 8443 上提供 HTTPS（请参阅安装 Jetty 和部署 WAR），因此任何构建绝对 URL 的功能（例如密码重置电子邮件）都将引用错误的端口，直到您登录后更新设置 > 系统设置下的 Https 端口字段。 如果您通过 IP 或真实主机名而不是 localhost 访问服务器，也请更新 FQDN。

回收安装目录的所有权

install-mariadb 在生成 jdbc.xml 后故意将 /usr/local/spenego 锁定为任何人，因此默认情况下没有其他东西需要对其进行写访问。 对于此开发设置，Jetty 将以您自己的用户身份运行，因此请回收它：

sudo chown -R "$USER":"$USER" /usr/local/spenego

安装 Jetty 并部署 WAR

export JETTY_HOME=/usr/local/spenego/jetty_home
export JETTY_BASE=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base

mkdir -p "$JETTY_HOME"
tar -xzf "$OBIDOS_SRC/dist/obidos/jetty_dist.tar.gz" -C "$JETTY_HOME" --strip-components=1

mkdir -p "$JETTY_BASE"
cd "$JETTY_BASE"
# start.d/ must exist *before* --add-to-start runs, otherwise Jetty falls
# back to writing everything into one monolithic start.ini instead of
# per-module files in start.d/, and start.d/ never gets created at all
mkdir -p "$JETTY_BASE/start.d"
java -jar "$JETTY_HOME/start.jar" --add-to-start=ssl,https,deploy,jsp,ext,resources,console-capture

最后一个命令是 Jetty 自己的引导机制。 它为您要求的模块创建 webapps/、lib/ext/、logs/、etc/ 和 start.d/*.ini 文件：TLS 连接器、WAR 自动部署、JSP 支持、额外的 jars 目录和控制台日志捕获。 未启用纯 HTTP 模块，请参阅“安装”部分中的 TLS 注释了解原因。

生成自签名证书

找到机器的 IP 地址，这是您将在证书中输入的内容，然后在浏览器的地址栏中输入：

ip a

在活动网络接口（例如 eth0 或 enp0s3）下查找 inet 行，而不是 lo（环回接口，127.0.0.1）。 例如，inet 192.168.1.213/24 ... 表示您的 IP 地址是 192.168.1.213。

上面的 --add-to-start=ssl 步骤已经将 Jetty 自己的演示密钥库复制到 $JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore。 首先将其删除，否则 keytool 将尝试使用演示密钥库自己的密码打开它，而不是创建一个新密码，并失败并显示“密钥库被篡改，或密码不正确”：

rm -f "$JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore"
keytool -genkeypair -alias jetty -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 3650 \
  -storetype PKCS12 -storepass changeit -keypass changeit \
  -keystore "$JETTY_BASE/etc/keystore" \
  -dname "CN=<IP-address>, OU=Obidos Eval, O=Obidos, L=NA, ST=NA, C=US"

将 <IP-address> 替换为您在上面找到的 IP 地址。 对于自签名证书，浏览器仍会显示“连接不是私有的”警告，这是预期的，请单击它（例如“高级”，然后单击“继续”）。

将 Jetty 的 SSL 模块指向此密钥库并绑定它以进行远程访问，该模块默认仅绑定 127.0.0.1：

cat > "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos-ssl.ini" <<'EOF'
jetty.ssl.host=0.0.0.0
jetty.ssl.port=8443
jetty.sslContext.keyStorePassword=changeit
jetty.sslContext.keyManagerPassword=changeit
EOF

现在添加 Obidos 需要的 JVM 标志，并部署 WAR：

cat > "$JETTY_BASE/start.d/99-obidos.ini" <<'EOF'
--exec
--add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens=java.base/java.lang.reflect=ALL-UNNAMED
EOF

注意：Jetty 的 start.jar 分叉一个子 JVM 来实际运行服务器。 如果您在命令行上传递 --add-opens ，则子 JVM 永远看不到它。 这些标志仅在来自与 --exec 结合使用的 start.ini/start.d 文件时才会生效，该文件告诉 Jetty 构建子 JVM 的命令行以包含它们。

cp "$OBIDOS_SRC"/target/Obidos-*.war "$JETTY_BASE/webapps/ROOT.war"
cp "$OBIDOS_SRC/dist/obidos/lib/javax.servlet-api-3.1.0.jar" "$JETTY_BASE/lib/ext/"

mkdir -p /usr/local/spenego/obidos/DataStore

注意，这里不需要scripts/fix_war.bash。 它修补了 WAR 的 cookie 域，以解决仅当 Jetty 和反向代理 (nginx) 设置 cookie 时才会发生的双 cookie 错误。 由于本指南直接与 Jetty 通信，前面没有代理，因此请跳过它，仅当您稍后将其放在 nginx 后面时才运行它。

注意：如果 Jetty 无法启动或日志记录看起来已损坏，则生产 jetty_base 会捆绑特定的 log4j + slf4j-log4j12 绑定（lib/log4j/log4j-1.2.17.jar、lib/slf4j/slf4j-log4j12-1.7.25.jar），而不是 Jetty 的默认日志记录模块。 如果遇到与 log4j/slf4j 相关的 NoClassDefFoundError，请将这两个 jar 也复制到 $JETTY_BASE/lib/ext/ 中。

将 Jetty 作为 systemd 服务运行

sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/obidos.service > /dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=Obidos (Jetty)
After=network.target mariadb.service
Requires=mariadb.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=$USER
Environment=JETTY_HOME=/usr/local/spenego/jetty_home
Environment=JETTY_BASE=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base
WorkingDirectory=/usr/local/spenego/obidos/jetty_base
ExecStart=/usr/bin/java -jar \${JETTY_HOME}/start.jar
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
